text:
maria: MistralHealth reporting sudden p99 spikes on embeddings API — started ~2026-02-12T16:12Z. They say p99 went from ~200ms to 6-8s and it's affecting their semantic search freshness. root request id: r-0a3c9f. Seen by CS during customer demo :grimacing: 

devon: ok pinging infra -- do we have model + region + recent deploy info? any correlated node OOMs or high NVLink pressure?

maria: customer payloads attached in their ticket — large batch of docs, some docs ~120k chars. Using hosted embeddings endpoint, model: text-embed-001-quant (older quantized variant). Region: us-west-2. They said this started after a 'performance' deploy at 16:00.

infra-bot: ALERT: embeddings-service.p99 > 3s avg across us-west-2 between 16:05 - 16:20. Top offending tenant: mistralhealth (tenant_id: t-mistral-99). Node cluster: emb-nodepool-7.

devon: quick hypothesis: long documents + huge batch = KV cache churn and kernel fallback on the quant model -> long tail for that node. Also we've seen heavier host CPU when GPU kernels fall back on older quantization paths. Can we get a sample request to repro? ask customer for smallest repro.

alex: I asked MistralHealth for a smaller repro; they shared this simplified payload that still causes a spike: 

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-mistral-99",
  "model": "text-embed-001-quant",
  "inputs": ["<very long doc>" repeated 3],
  "batch_size": 512
}
```

maria: they said they send nightly bulk ingestion and hit spike when ingest overlap + interactive search traffic. Want an allowlist so their ingestion doesn't get throttled/queued — they argue it's critical.

devon: two tracks: short-term mitigation + longer-term correctness. Short term we can: 
- route their traffic to nodes with higher preemption priority? (we have a node pool with Dedicated-shared lanes)
- temporarily add them to a bespoke reservation/allowlist for the night window (this increases their cost risk and reduces isolation).
- enforce max_batch_size and per-request token cap at the gateway (we can do this unilaterally).

sam: Routing note: we have a spare small cluster in us-east-1 with matching kernels. Could we transparently route their heavy batch jobs there for a few hours? Need to check data residency. Also, the quant variant has known pathologies on seq_len > 16k — we can route them to the non-quant variant for large-doc batches.

devon: agree — recommended immediate steps: 
1) Apply temporary per-tenant token cap: 50k tokens per request for t-mistral-99. This will prevent huge single requests from thrashing KV.
2) Create temporary routing rule: if request.model == "text-embed-001-quant" and tokens > 8k then route to text-embed-001 (full FP) in us-east-1.
3) Give customer a one-night reservation window (capacity ticket) for their nightly job: reservation id R-314159. We need billing OK from finance before committing.

maria: customer accepted token cap if we give them a scheduled reservation window + SLA for that night. They asked what to change client-side (they prefer not to split jobs manually).

alex: suggested client changes: batch smaller (<=128), chunk docs >8k tokens, use async ingestion job with exponential backoff on 429/503. Sent them a small snippet: 

```python
# recommended client-side chunking
for doc in docs:
    for chunk in chunker(doc, max_tokens=8000):
        client.embed(model="text-embed-001", inputs=[chunk])
```

infra-bot: ACTION CREATED: support/12384 - Temporary reservation R-314159 requested for t-mistral-99. Assigned to sam.

sam: starting routing rule change now. I'll also spin up a small dedicated subgroup in us-east-1 and add a preemption tag. ETA ~ 18 minutes.

devon: I'll push a gateway patch to enforce per-request token cap + batch size cap for that tenant. Patch will be a hotfix on gateway: 

```yaml
match:
  tenant_id: t-mistral-99
action:
  max_tokens_per_request: 50000
  max_batch_size: 128
  route_overrides:
    - condition: request.model == "text-embed-001-quant" and request.tokens > 8000
      route_to: us-east-1/text-embed-001
```

maria: tracking customer comms: told them we'll pause ingestion if they push >50k tokens after 3 warnings. They're ok.

infra-bot: DEPLOY: gateway-hotfix-v2 to production at 16:40Z by devon - success.

devon: observed immediate drop in p99 on emb-nodepool-7 from ~6s -> 350ms after the route override + caps. us-west-2 still has occasional spikes correlated with interactive traffic but much reduced.

maria: customer reported their demo completed once we put the reservation and caps in place. They asked for a permanent solution because nightly ingest is core.

sam: long-term options for MistralHealth: 
- promote them to Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) with controlled GPU variants for bulk ingest.
- provide an SDK helper to auto-chunk and switch model variants for large docs.
- add model-variant auto-routing based on tokens/seq_len (we already prototyped this).

alex: I'll schedule a post-mortem with the CS and SRE owners to document the incident, root cause (quant variant fallback under large seq/batch), and recommended billing/reservation flow. Also propose a new telemetry alert: per-tenant average tokens/request > 10k for >5min to preemptively notify CS.

maria: thanks everyone — action items from thread: 
- devon: gateway patch (done) and post-incident notes (assign).
- sam: reservation R-314159 setup and routing change (in progress).
- alex: customer SDK snippet + follow-up doc for chunking.
- maria: confirm billing approval and send customer final plan.

infra-bot: TICKET UPDATE: support/12384 -> reservation provisioned (R-314159) at 17:02Z.

devon: closing loop — I'll attach kernel metrics + flame graph showing the fallback path for the quant model to the post-mortem. Putting this thread into incidents for the record.

maria: closing with customer confirmed success. We'll reopen if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:
